title: Transit-access score definition + methodology (walk threshold, network, frequency)
context: A transit-access explainer must be built on a locked, peer-reviewed definition of what 'transit access' means. Without a precise methodology committed before any metro explainer is built, the score can be gamed, compared incorrectly across metros, or misread as a 'good/bad place' judgement. The methodology must define the walk-distance threshold, network vs. straight-line measurement, and frequency weighting — and explicitly state what the score does NOT claim.
objective: Define and lock the transit-access score methodology (walk threshold, network vs. straight-line, frequency weighting, and explicit non-claims), reviewed and signed off by the Methodology+Stats and Domain (transport) reviewers before any metro explainer begins.
acceptanceCriteria: A committed methodology document defines: (a) the walk-distance threshold in metres or minutes, (b) whether the score uses network routing or straight-line distance to stops, (c) the frequency weighting approach (e.g. peak departures per hour), and (d) an explicit list of what the score does NOT claim (no 'good/bad place' judgement, no causal claims).
Methodology Card schema (methodcard-004) completed for the transit-access module.
Methodology+Stats reviewer and Domain (transport) reviewer sign-offs obtained and committed.
No metro explainer (transit-015 or any per-region fan-out) may proceed until this task is done.
resources: PLAN.md — Open questions section (transit-access score definition)
PLAN.md — Quality, review & risk gates section (Methodology+Stats gate)
output: A committed transit-access score methodology document (transit-methodology.md + Methodology Card JSON), locked with Methodology+Stats and Domain reviewer sign-offs, blocking any metro explainer until done.
